theorem: For EVERY PPT nonnegative diagonal weighted 2024 5x5 grid source, and EVERY rank-four map on either local subsystem whose kernel is contained in span{|h>,|t>} for any h in {0,1,2}, t in {3,4}, the resulting 4x5 or 5x4 state has SN<=2. Any further local map on the opposite side preserves this bound. This covers all six complete complex head-tail CP1 families on each subsystem and arbitrary weights, not only the original state. Any local kernel lying in the head span{|0>,|1>,|2>} also trivially gives SN<=2 without PPT. For the original trace18 PPT/SN3 grid, the previously proved balanced tail CP1 supplies the remaining two-sparse tail-tail case, so any two-sparse kernel on either side followed by an arbitrary opposite map gives PPT/SN<=2.
source_and_ppt_inputs: Use https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12966v1 Figure 2: A=|02>+|11>+|20>, V=|01>, W=|10>, B=|12>+|34>, C=|21>+|43>, loops F=|32>, G=|41>, H=|14>, J=|23>, and the other SR<=2 generators |00> and Q=|22>+|33>. Let alpha,beta,delta,b,c,f,g,h,j be their nonnegative weights in this order. PPT implies beta*b>=alpha^2 from |01>,|12>; delta*c>=alpha^2 from |10>,|21>; h*f>=b^2 from |14>,|32>; and j*g>=c^2 from |23>,|41>. If alpha=0, all generators are already SR<=2. For alpha>0 the displayed weights needed below are positive. Normalize a mixed kernel by K|head>=|head>, K|tail>=r|head>, and preserve the other basis states; r in C. Coordinate endpoints follow from the earlier coordinate-cut theorem or the trivial head-support argument.
direct_cases_04_23: For head0/tail4, C'=|21>+r|03>, W'=|10>, and A' is unchanged. For z^4=1, q_z=sqrt(alpha)*A'+z*sqrt(delta)*W'+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(delta))*C' has SR<=2 because its rows1,2 are proportional, including arbitrary complex r in row0. Its phase average consumes alpha[A']+delta[W']+alpha^2/delta[C']; PPT makes the residual C weight nonnegative. For head2/tail3, B'=|12>+r|24>, V'=|01>. Replace W,delta,C,c by V,beta,B,b: rows0,1 are proportional and beta*b>=alpha^2 makes the residual nonnegative. All other projected generators have SR<=2.
overlapping_product_cases_13_24: For head1/tail3 put R=|r|^2, X=|12>, Y=|14>; B'=X+rY, F'=rX, H'=Y and V'=|01>. The phase seed sqrt(alpha)A'+z*sqrt(beta)V'+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(beta))X has SR<=2. After its phase average, the remaining B',F',H' sector is the 2x2 Gram [[b+fR-alpha^2/beta,b*conjugate(r)],[b*r,bR+h]] on (X,Y). Its Schur complement equals b-alpha^2/beta+R*(f-b^2/(h+bR))>=0 by beta*b>=alpha^2 and h*f>=b^2. Every vector in span(X,Y) is product because both have the same Alice factor. For head2/tail4 use X=|21>, Y=|23>, C'=X+rY, G'=rX, J'=Y, W'=|10>; the same argument applies after replacing (beta,b,f,h) by (delta,c,g,j).
two_seed_case_03: For head0/tail3 and r!=0, set R=|r|^2, X=|02>, F'=rX, B'=|12>+r|04>, V'=|01>, H'=|14>; A' is unchanged. Put s=alpha/(alpha+fR), p=1-s, lambda=fR/alpha, beta0=beta/s, k=alpha/sqrt(beta*s), and h0=alpha^(3/2)*r/beta. The rank2 vector q0=sqrt(alpha)*(A'-X). For z^4=1 define q_z=sqrt(alpha)*(A'+lambda X)+z*sqrt(beta0)V'+conjugate(z)*k B'+z^2*h0 H'. Its row0 is (z*sqrt(beta0)/sqrt(alpha)) times row1, with row2 independent; this uses z^3=conjugate(z), k*sqrt(beta0)=alpha*(1+lambda), and h0=k*r*sqrt(alpha/beta0). Thus SR(q_z)<=2. The mixture p[q0]+(s/4)sum[q_z] consumes alpha[A']+f[F']+beta[V']+(alpha^2/beta)[B']+(s*alpha^3*R/beta^2)[H']. All source residuals are nonnegative: b>=alpha^2/beta, and s*alpha^3*R/beta^2=alpha^4*R/(beta^2*(alpha+fR))<=h because beta*b>=alpha^2 and h*f>=b^2. Other projected source generators remain SR<=2.
two_seed_case_14: For head1/tail4 use X=|11>, G'=rX, C'=|21>+r|13>, W'=|10>, J'=|23>. Repeat the preceding construction with (V,beta,B,b,F,f,H,h) replaced by (W,delta,C,c,G,g,J,j). The two PPT minors delta*c>=alpha^2 and j*g>=c^2 give the same nonnegative residual bounds. This handles r!=0; coordinate endpoints follow separately.
bob_and_composition: Factor swap maps the whole weighted source family into itself, exchanging (V,beta,B,b,F,f,H,h) with (W,delta,C,c,G,g,J,j), and preserves PPT. It therefore transfers all six Alice results to Bob. Subsequent arbitrary opposite local maps and invertible output coordinate changes preserve a nonnegative SR2 decomposition. The head CP2 assertion holds because a rank-four map whose kernel lies in the head support makes A' rank<=2 and every other source generator already has rank<=2.
original_two_sparse_consequence: The original source has alpha=beta=delta=b=c=q=1, so the balanced-tail theorem frontier-20261028-grid55-balanced-full-tail-v1.json SHA256 602c6ce2ee29708732878e705f83077b4be5dc5c8420e22e70542a56ace82d41 covers tail span{|3>,|4>} on either side. Combining it with all six head-tail CP1 families and the trivial head CP2 gives SN<=2 for every original-source rank-four map with any two-sparse kernel, with an arbitrary opposite map. This does not imply SN<=2 for generic kernels.

exact_checks.observed: For each of the six lines, the checker evaluates a nontrivial exact r (r=2 for 03, r=3/4 for 14, and r=1+i otherwise), all phase-vector rank minors, 400 actual Alice output entries, its PT, all 400 direct Bob output entries and its PT. For the symmetric original source it also checks each Bob output equals the tensor swap of the Alice output. It hash-pins and replays six earlier r=1 checks on both subsystems. General complex r and all weighted PPT inputs follow from the written four cases and PPT minors, not the samples.

limits: The six full head-tail families are proven only for this specified PPT weighted 5x5 grid. The tail-tail claim for arbitrary weights remains conditional on the separate balance hypothesis. Generic kernel lines and arbitrary 4x4 PPT states, an SN>=3 target witness, external/formal review and novelty remain open.
